title: Rod of Absorption vs Diluvian Primordial: same replacement goal, so no conflict
question: You control Rod of Absorption and cast Diluvian Primordial. When you cast an instant or sorcery with the Primordial's trigger, where does that spell go as it finishes resolving?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: It's exiled under Rod of Absorption. Diluvian Primordial's ability exiles the spell instead of letting it go to a graveyard, and Rod of Absorption's ability does the same thing for that specific case. Both have the same goal, so there is no conflict and the spell is exiled under Rod of Absorption as normal.
notes: Ask a Magic Judge (magicjudge.tumblr.com), judge-run rules blog; post 728634630741360640 fetched via the Tumblr read API 2026-10-12. Question/answer paraphrased (short) from the post. Distinguishes two replacement effects that both exile the resolving spell (they agree, so no ordering conflict).

title: Oskar, Rubbish Reclaimer + Dream Halls: alternate cost works from the graveyard
question: You control Oskar, Rubbish Reclaimer and Dream Halls. Can you cast a card you discarded to Oskar by discarding a card that shares a color with it instead of paying its mana cost?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Yes. Dream Halls doesn't care where the spell is being cast from, so its alternate cost can pay for cards you discarded with Oskar. Note that Oskar's trigger resolves before the spell it lets you cast, so chaining this puts several spells on the stack at once, and Oskar's cast happens right away so timing restrictions don't apply.

title: Mutate can't target a permanent you don't own
question: You gain access to an opponent's creature with mutate (say Vulpikeet, granted by Draugr Necromancer). Can you cast it for its mutate cost targeting a creature you own?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: No. A spell cast for its mutate cost can only ever target a permanent with the same owner as that card, so you can't merge their creature onto one of yours.

title: Backup is a triggered ability, so Killian doesn't reduce it
question: You control Killian, Ink Duelist. Do creature spells with backup cost 2 less to cast?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: No. Backup is a triggered ability that triggers once the creature is on the battlefield. A creature spell on the stack never targets anything unless it's a card cast for its mutate cost, so Killian's cost reduction doesn't apply.

title: Awaken the Blood Avatar + Poxwalkers: the creature returns during casting
question: You cast Awaken the Blood Avatar from exile (not your hand) and sacrifice Poxwalkers as part of the additional cost. Does the sacrificed Poxwalkers' return-to-battlefield ability trigger?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Yes. A spell isn't considered to be cast until the whole casting process is complete, and paying the costs is part of that process. Because Awaken the Blood Avatar was cast from somewhere other than your hand, the sacrificed Poxwalkers' ability triggers.

title: Deathtouch applies to noncombat damage too (Cosmic Hunger)
question: A creature you control with deathtouch deals damage equal to its power to another target creature via Cosmic Hunger. Does deathtouch apply?

title: Shelob vs a noncreature planeswalker: a Legendary Artifact - Food with loyalty abilities
question: Shelob, Child of Ungoliant kills a planeswalker that had been turned into a creature. What token does Shelob make, and can that token use loyalty abilities?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Shelob makes a token copy of the printed card except it's an Artifact - Food instead of its other types. If the killed permanent was a planeswalker (e.g. Sarkhan the Masterless), the token is a Legendary Artifact - Food that enters with no loyalty counters (only planeswalkers enter with loyalty). It isn't a planeswalker, so it can't be attacked and won't die for having 0 loyalty, but its loyalty abilities still work normally.

title: Nahiri's +1 vs Ghostly Prison: requirements beat restrictions
question: You control Nahiri, the Unforgiving and Ghostly Prison, and use Nahiri's +1 to force an opponent's creature to attack you. Can its controller simply decline to attack because of the Prison tax?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: No. When a player declares attackers they must satisfy the maximum number of requirements possible without violating any restrictions. The creature is required to attack a player, and if it can attack another player without paying a cost, declining does not meet that maximum. It could decline only if every opponent had a Ghostly Prison-style effect.

title: Tribute to the World Tree checks power as its trigger resolves
question: A 2-power creature enters while another creature's enters-the-battlefield trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on it before Tribute's trigger resolves. Do you draw a card or put two +1/+1 counters on the creature?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Tribute to the World Tree's trigger checks the creature's power only as it resolves. If the power has changed by then, the new power determines which effect you get. If the creature has left the battlefield, its last-known power is used.

title: Ward and 'becomes the target': redirecting can't double-trigger one permanent
question: You redirect an opponent's spell to your creature with ward using Deflecting Swat. Does ward trigger, and can you trigger it extra times by redirecting again?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Ward triggers only when the permanent goes from not being a target to being a target. Redirecting the spell to your creature makes it a new target, so ward triggers. But choosing the same target again, or adding it as an additional target, won't trigger ward again. To make someone pay ward multiple times you must move the target between two different ward permanents.
notes: Ask a Magic Judge (magicjudge.tumblr.com), judge-run rules blog; post 724559624609644544 fetched via the Tumblr read API 2026-10-12. Question/answer paraphrased (short) from the post.

title: A noncreature ring-bearer stays your ring-bearer if you have no other creatures
question: Mutavault becomes a creature, the ring tempts you and you make it your ring-bearer, then it stops being a creature. The next time the ring tempts you, do you lose your ring-bearer?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Being a ring-bearer is a status a permanent keeps until you choose another creature as ring-bearer or lose control of it, and it doesn't require the permanent to remain a creature. So you must choose a different creature if you control one, but if you control no other creature, Mutavault remains your ring-bearer.
notes: Ask a Magic Judge (magicjudge.tumblr.com), judge-run rules blog; post 724557753586237440 fetched via the Tumblr read API 2026-10-12. Question/answer paraphrased (short) from the post. The ring-tempt mechanic is from The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth (2023).

title: Ob Nixilis, Captive Kingpin counts one 'deals' event, not one per creature
question: Your opponent controls several creatures and resolves Rakdos Charm's third mode (each creature deals 1 damage to its controller). How many times does Ob Nixilis, Captive Kingpin trigger?

answer: Zero. Rakdos Charm uses the verb 'deals' once, so it's a single damage event; with no modifiers the result is each player losing life equal to the number of creatures they control. Your opponent loses more than 1 life, so Ob Nixilis (which triggers only when they lose exactly 1 life) doesn't trigger.

title: Blitz's delayed sacrifice survives the creature losing its abilities

title: Stun counters turn an untap cost into removing the counter
question: How do stun counters interact with abilities that use the untap symbol as a cost?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: A stun counter creates a replacement effect that removes the counter instead of untapping the permanent the next time it would untap. Because paying an untap-symbol cost untaps the permanent, that payment is replaced by removing a stun counter, the permanent stays tapped, and the ability can be activated again. With three stun counters you could activate such an ability up to four times in a turn.
notes: Ask a Magic Judge (magicjudge.tumblr.com), judge-run rules blog; post 722757134844051456 fetched via the Tumblr read API 2026-10-12. Question/answer paraphrased (short) from the post.

title: Saheeli's Lattice craft: a commander in the command zone isn't in exile
question: Anthony activates the craft ability of Saheeli's Lattice, exiling a Pathfinding Axejaw (which had a +1/+1 counter) and his commander Gishath, Sun's Avatar, choosing to move the commander to the command zone. What is Mastercraft Raptor's power once the craft ability resolves?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: 4. Mastercraft Raptor looks at the power of the cards in exile. Pathfinding Axejaw lost its +1/+1 counter when it left the battlefield, so its power in exile is 4, and Gishath isn't in exile (the command-zone choice means the static ability can't get information about it even though it was briefly in exile, CR 702.167c). So the only contributing card is Pathfinding Axejaw at power 4.
notes: Judge Foundry 'The Lost Caverns of Ixalan update quiz wrapup' (Jan 25, 2024), Q2245, by Exams Manager John Brian McCarthy; cited CR 702.167c. Fetched 2026-10-12.

title: Fabricate is a trigger: a removed Marionette Apprentice makes a Servo
question: Andrea resolves Marionette Apprentice and announces she'll put a +1/+1 counter on it when the fabricate trigger resolves. In response, Nate activates Barbarian Ring's last ability to deal 2 damage to Marionette Apprentice, destroying it. What happens when the fabricate trigger resolves?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Andrea creates a 1/1 Servo token. Fabricate is a triggered ability and the choice isn't made until the trigger resolves (CR 117.5), so Nate can respond and remove the creature. When the trigger resolves Andrea can't put a +1/+1 counter on the now-absent Apprentice (even though she announced that choice before Nate responded), so she creates a Servo (CR 702.123a, CR 118.12).
notes: Judge Foundry 'Modern Horizons 3 Update Quiz Wrapup' (Aug 19, 2024), Q2863, by Judge John Brian McCarthy; cited CR 117.5, 702.123a, 118.12. Fetched 2026-10-12.

title: Blacksmith's Talent + Flowerfoot Swordmaster + Heartfire Hero: damage across two combat damage steps
question: Anita controls Blacksmith's Talent at level 3, a Sword Equipment token (equipped to Heartfire Hero, which has no counters), Flowerfoot Swordmaster, and Heartfire Hero, and Nedra doesn't block. Anita casts Valley Rally with gift targeting the Swordmaster; at beginning of combat the Talent's trigger targets the Sword token and Heartfire Hero; then she attacks with all. How much damage does Anita deal in each combat damage step?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: In the first combat damage step Heartfire Hero deals 6 and Flowerfoot Swordmaster deals 4; in the second combat damage step Heartfire Hero deals 6 again. Valley Rally gave both Mouse creatures +2/+0 (so Flowerfoot is a 4/2) and first strike, the Swordmaster's valiant trigger added another +1/+0, and the Blacksmith's Talent trigger targeting Heartfire Hero added a +1/+1 counter (making it a 6/3 with double strike); the judge explanation cites CR 608.2c.
notes: Judge Foundry 'Bloomburrow quiz wrapup' (Oct 2, 2024), Q2979, by Judge John Brian McCarthy; cited CR 608.2c. Fetched 2026-10-12.

title: Protection from everything: a spell that targets you has all targets illegal and fizzles
question: You control The One Ring and have protection from everything. What happens to a spell or ability that targets you, and does protection stop damage and non-targeted effects?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Protection from everything means all damage that would be dealt to you is prevented, Auras can't be attached to you, and you can't be the target of spells or abilities. A spell or ability on the stack that targets you then has an illegal target; if all its targets are illegal it doesn't resolve and none of its effects happen (including effects unrelated to the target). It is not a blanket prevention of non-targeted effects: you can still be made to discard, and creatures can still attack you (though their combat damage is prevented).
notes: Wizards official ruling for The One Ring (LTR 246), fetched 2026-10-12 via api.scryfall.com/cards/ltr/246/rulings.

title: Orcish Bowmasters: 'put into hand' without 'draw' is not a card drawn
question: Your opponent is forced to put cards into their hand by an effect that doesn't use the word 'draw'. Does Orcish Bowmasters trigger?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: No, if the effect doesn't specifically use the word 'draw' it isn't a card drawn, so the 'whenever an opponent draws a card' trigger won't fire. Relatedly, when amassing Orcs with no Army, the token enters as a 0/0 creature before receiving counters, so enters-the-battlefield abilities that check power see it as 0/0.
notes: Wizards official ruling for Orcish Bowmasters (LTR 103), fetched 2026-10-12 via api.scryfall.com/cards/ltr/103/rulings.

title: Roaming Throne adds an extra trigger; two Thrones triple it
question: You control Roaming Throne (choosing a creature type) and a creature of that type with a triggered ability. How many times does the ability trigger, and what about two Thrones?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: Roaming Throne's last ability doesn't copy the triggered ability; it just causes it to trigger an additional time, and any choices (modes and targets) are made separately for each instance. With two Roaming Thrones that share the same chosen creature type, another creature's triggered abilities of that type trigger three times (three Thrones give four, and so on).
notes: Wizards official ruling for Roaming Throne (LCI 258), fetched 2026-10-12 via api.scryfall.com/cards/lci/258/rulings.

title: Guide of Souls's reflexive ability picks its target only after you pay energy
question: You attack with Guide of Souls and pay {E}{E}{E} to its attack trigger. When is the target chosen, and how long does the type-changing effect last?
board_state: described in the question (no separate board state)
answer: You don't choose a target for the last ability when it triggers; rather, a second 'reflexive' ability triggers when you pay the energy, and you choose its target as that ability goes on the stack, so players can respond to it normally. The type-changing effect of that reflexive ability lasts indefinitely - it doesn't wear off during the cleanup step or if Guide of Souls leaves the battlefield.
notes: Wizards official ruling for Guide of Souls (MH3 29), fetched 2026-10-12 via api.scryfall.com/cards/mh3/29/rulings.
